question: A 30-year-old man presents with acute-onset, unilateral, non-granulomatous anterior uveitis with severe ciliary flush, aqueous cells, and fine KPs. He gives a history of lower back pain that is worse at rest and improves with activity. Which systemic association should be prioritised in this patient's workup?

answers.text: Sarcoidosis — the most common cause of non-granulomatous anterior uveitis in young men

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sarcoidosis classically causes GRANULOMATOUS uveitis (mutton-fat KPs, iris nodules, chronic course). It does not typically present as acute unilateral non-granulomatous uveitis. Additionally, the inflammatory back pain (worse at rest, better with activity) strongly points elsewhere.

answers.text: HLA-B27-associated spondyloarthropathy (ankylosing spondylitis) — acute, unilateral, non-granulomatous anterior uveitis with inflammatory back pain is the classic pattern

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Acute, unilateral, recurrent, non-granulomatous anterior uveitis is the ophthalmic hallmark of HLA-B27-associated disease. Inflammatory back pain (worse at night/rest, improves with exercise) is the cardinal feature of ankylosing spondylitis. Roughly 25–40% of HLA-B27-positive patients will have at least one episode of anterior uveitis. Order HLA-B27 typing and rheumatology referral.

answers.text: Behçet disease — characterised by recurrent anterior uveitis and shifting hypopyon

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Behçet disease does cause recurrent uveitis but characteristically affects BOTH eyes, produces posterior or panuveitis with retinal vasculitis, and is associated with oral aphthous ulcers and genital ulcers — not inflammatory back pain. The clinical picture here is more consistent with HLA-B27-associated disease.

answers.text: Tuberculosis — the back pain suggests vertebral TB (Pott's disease) with sympathetic uveitis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. TB uveitis is granulomatous (mutton-fat KPs, choroidal granulomas). Pott's disease causes MECHANICAL back pain from bone destruction, not the inflammatory back pain pattern (worse at rest, better with activity) described. The non-granulomatous pattern and inflammatory back pain point strongly to HLA-B27-associated spondyloarthropathy.

overallFeedback.feedback: The pattern of acute, unilateral, non-granulomatous anterior uveitis combined with inflammatory back pain (worse at rest, better with movement) is classic for HLA-B27-associated spondyloarthropathy. Sarcoid and TB cause granulomatous disease; Behçet causes bilateral disease with additional mucocutaneous features.

Correct. Acute unilateral non-granulomatous anterior uveitis + inflammatory back pain = HLA-B27 workup first. Ankylosing spondylitis is the prototype; also consider reactive arthritis (Reiter's), psoriatic arthritis, and IBD-associated arthropathy.
